thread:
kevin: FYI noticed a host-side perf regression after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak. Small-chat p95 up ~60% on canaries, CPU on ingress boxes jumped. :frowning_face:

nina: Can you paste the numbers and a short repro? is this only small requests or wide traffic? :eyes:

kevin: Only seen in small requests (<128 tokens). Numbers from canary cluster: before: p95=28ms, mean=12ms. after: p95=45ms, mean=18ms. kernel_picker invocation count per request went from ~0.6 to ~1.0 (i.e. now running per request more often).

kevin: Quick flame from perf (sampled on a hotspot box):
```
50.0%  parse_frame
20.0%  tokenize_utf8
15.0%  kernel_selector::score
10.0%  kv_cache::lookup_lock
```

alaric: Hmm kernel_selector::score at 15% is suspicious. Did the picker switch from cached buckets to live scoring?

kevin: Yeah, we introduced a sequence-length-aware scoring pass that checks batch shape at request time. Looks like we forgot to memoize it per model+batch_key.

maya: That scoring was meant to improve kernel quality for longer tails, but it shouldn't run on every tiny request. Suggest caching score results keyed by (model, max_seq_len_bucket, hw_tag) for 30s.

nina: Agreed. Also kv_cache::lookup_lock at 10% suggests contention. That may be because requests are slightly slower so more concurrent lookups pile up. Fixing picker should reduce that secondary effect.

kevin: Quick patch idea — add an in-memory LRU inside kernel_picker with TTL and a fast-path if batch_count==1 and seq_len<64 skip scoring. Pseudo-config: 
```
kernel_picker:
  cache_ttl_ms: 30000
  min_seq_for_scoring: 64
  max_entries: 4096
```

alaric: +1. Also consider moving scoring off the hot request path into the batching threadpool. Compute score async and use last-known-good while computing. That reduces tail risk.

maya: Can you try turning off dynamic scoring via flag to confirm? `kernel_picker.disable_dynamic=true`

kevin: Just ran a smoke test with the flag on a replica set: p95 dropped to 30ms, flame shows kernel_selector at 3% now. So that's the culprit.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started by @kevin for service=ingress-host-parse, image=ingress:v2024-06-21-patch1 :rocket:

nina: Good repro. Two follow-ups: 1) implement TTL LRU patch, 2) add unit + microbench for scoring path to prevent reintroduction. Also add telemetry metric `kernel_picker.cache_hit` and `kernel_picker.duration_ms`.

kevin: I'll land the TTL LRU patch + metric tonight and run a 2h canary. If green, we roll to prod tomorrow morning.

alaric: One more note: check gRPC/HTTP framing overhead when you test. If small requests get slower, the fixed handshakes matter more. Try enabling writev coalescing on the proxy if we still see small regressions.

kevin: Noted — will include a small A/B with `proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true` to validate.

maya: Thanks — great catch. tagging infra on-call if we see CPU alarms during canary: @nina please ping if >10% CPU delta sustained. :thumbsup:

kevin: Will do. Opening a short PR and linking perf traces. https://internal.perf/trace/1766660000 (contains pprof + flamegraphs)

nina: :eyes: once PR lands add a benchmark job to CI that runs the small-request profile so this doesn't regress silently.

kevin: On it.

(reacts: maya :thumbsup:, alaric :rocket:)
